240	- Remediation: build the child env from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, project-declared
241	  vars) and strip Nexus's own credential vars (`LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`) unless the operator opts in;
242	  also tokenise values of env vars whose names match `KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD` in tool output.
243	- Acceptance test: with `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY=REDACTED set, `run_command env` output does not contain `x123456789`.
244	
245	### T11 run_tests: filter is shell-injected, executes without approval, and is scheduled as a parallel "read-only" tool
246	- Priority: P1
247	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
248	- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
249	- Observed: `detectTestCommand` interpolates the model-supplied `filter` into a shell string — unquoted for Cargo
250	  (`cargo test -- ${filterPattern}`, tester.ts:37) and inside naive double quotes for make/npm/pytest/go (:30, :47, :55,
251	  :60). `run_tests` calls `this.executeTool("run_command", …)` directly (tools.ts:556-561), bypassing the agent's
252	  approval prompt, which never includes `run_tests` (agent.ts:2503-2508). `run_tests` is also in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`
253	  (agent.ts:378-389) and capabilities marks it `mutating: false` (capabilities.ts:788-790), so it runs concurrently with
254	  other tools via `Promise.all` (agent.ts:3186-3194) and does not bump `mutationSeq` (agent.ts:744-749).
255	  ```
256	  ws3/package.json: {"scripts":{"test":"echo tests-ran"}}
257	  tsx probe_runtests.mts ws3   (RustCoreBridge(ws3).executeTool("run_tests", {filter: 'x" ; touch INJECTED_BY_FILTER ; echo "'}))
258	  command: npm test -- -t "x" ; touch INJECTED_BY_FILTER ; echo ""
259	  success: true
260	  ls ws3 -> INJECTED_BY_FILTER  package.json
261	  ```
262	  The trailing `echo ""` also makes the exit status 0, so a failing suite can be recorded as a PASSED verifier
263	  attempt (agent.ts:2623-2634 records status from `parsed.passed && receipt.success`).
264	- Impact: approval bypass for arbitrary shell; forged verifier passes; test runs that write files racing with
265	  parallel reads, unnoticed by staleness tracking.
266	- Remediation: pass the filter as an argv element (no shell) or reject anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_:./ -]`; treat
267	  run_tests as mutating/proc (remove from READ_ONLY_TOOLS; bump mutationSeq); route it through the same approval policy
268	  as run_command; record verifier attempts only for the configured, unfiltered command.
269	- Acceptance test: the probe above leaves no `INJECTED_BY_FILTER` and returns an argument-validation error; agent test
270	  shows `run_tests` + `read_file` in one response are executed sequentially.
271	
272	### T12 Parallel read-only path skips the cancellation check and output folding
273	- Priority: P3
274	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
275	- Observed: the sequential path checks `signal.aborted` before each dispatch (agent.ts:3225-3235) and folds voluminous
276	  run_command/run_tests output (:3261-3268); the parallel path (:3186-3218) does neither, so a cancelled turn still
277	  dispatches every parallel call and an unfolded `run_tests` result goes to context. The RPC daemon has no cancel verb
278	  (acknowledged in agent.ts:2707), so in-flight commands always run to their own timeout after cancel.
279	- Remediation: check `signal.aborted` before `Promise.all`; apply `foldVoluminousOutput` identically; add a `cancel`
280	  RPC that `killpg`s the request's process group.
281	- Acceptance test: cancel during a 2-call parallel batch -> both calls get `cancelledToolMessage`; cancel during
282	  `run_command sleep 30` returns within 1 s and no `sleep` survives.
283	
284	### T13 Dry-run executes "read-only-looking" commands unsandboxed; the allow-regex is prefix-only
285	- Priority: P2
286	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
287	- Observed: in dry-run, commands matching `SAFE_READONLY_COMMAND_REGEX` (tools.ts:31-32, anchored only at the start)
288	  fall through to real execution (tools.ts:524-532); `echo x > file`, `ls; rm -rf build`, `find . -delete`,
289	  `git diff --output=f` all match. Read-only mode is protected by the sandbox requirement (tools.ts:695-716), but dry-run
290	  is not wrapped unless a sandbox is configured.
291	  Reproduced (tp/main/cli/probe_dryrun.mts, `new RustCoreBridge(ws4, "bash", undefined, true)`):
292	  `echo x > DRYRUN_WROTE_THIS -> success, real run_command JSON result`; `touch NOT_ALLOWED -> [DRY-RUN SIMULATION]`;
293	  `ls ws4 -> DRYRUN_WROTE_THIS`.
294	- Remediation: in dry-run, never execute; or require the sandbox with `readOnlyHost` as read-only mode does.
295	- Acceptance test: dry-run `run_command "echo x > f"` -> simulated, `f` absent.
296	
297	
298	### T14 spawn_subagent: "isolated" helper shares the workspace and its tool calls skip the approval prompt
299	- Priority: P1
300	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
301	- Affects: all branches / installed runtime (REPL review mode and TUI approvals)
302	- Observed: without an active worktree the subagent config is `{...this.config}` with the same workspace
303	  (agent.ts:2195-2210) although the spinner says "Spawning isolated subagent". `runSubagent` dispatches every call as
304	  `dispatchToolCall(call, currentStep, "subagent")` with no `onConfirm` (agent.ts:3648), and the approval gate only runs
305	  when `onConfirm` is passed (agent.ts:2502-2508). So in review mode (`autoApprove=false`, repl.ts:282) or with TUI
306	  approvals (sidecar.ts:391-421), the parent's `spawn_subagent` call is not prompted (not in the gate list) and the
307	  child's `write_file`/`edit_file`/`run_command` run unprompted. Child edits also do not bump the parent's
308	  `mutationSeq` or call `invalidateVerified` (only `turnMutations`/`unverifiedChanges` are propagated, agent.ts:2238-2246),
309	  so a requirement already marked `verified` keeps that status in the ledger (and export) after a child edits the
310	  deliverable; a *new* verification is still blocked because the candidate identity changes (agent.ts:1480-1490).
311	- Impact: approval policy bypass by delegation; ledger shows "verified" for a changed deliverable until a later parent
312	  mutation demotes it.
313	- Remediation: pass the parent's `onConfirm` to the child (or force the child read-only unless a worktree is
314	  bound); include `spawn_subagent` in the approval gate; on child mutations call `invalidateVerified` and bump
315	  `mutationSeq` in the parent's `finally`.
316	- Acceptance test: mock-gateway agent test (pattern of cli/test/context_capacity_runtask.test.ts): parent calls
317	  `spawn_subagent`, child calls `write_file`; with an `onConfirm` that denies, the file is absent; with a requirement
318	  previously `verified`, after the child write its status is `implemented`.

320	### T15 list_dir, file_tree and cst_symbols are not confined to the workspace
321	- Priority: P2
322	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
323	- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
324	- Observed: these use `base_dir.join(&args.path)` (core/src/search.rs:67 list_dir, :387 file_tree; core/src/cst.rs:146)
325	  instead of `resolve_safe_path` (used by read/write/edit/delete/patch/file_info/batch_read and outline_file). The TS
326	  bridge's protected-path check covers only write/edit/patch/delete/read (tools.ts:432-441).
327	  ```
328	  $HC -w ws5 call --tool list_dir  --args '{"path":"../outside_secret"}' -> entries: "../outside_secret/creds.txt"
329	  $HC -w ws5 call --tool list_dir  --args '{"path":"/etc/ssh"}'          -> "/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key", ...
330	  $HC -w ws5 call --tool file_tree --args '{"path":"../outside_secret"}' -> tree "../outside_secret\n└── creds.txt"
331	  $HC -w ws5 call --tool outline_file --args '{"path":"../outside_secret/creds.txt"}' -> Security Violation (confined, for contrast)
332	  ```
333	  These are read-only parallel tools, so they also run without approval.
334	- Impact: host filesystem enumeration (names, sizes) outside the jail; inconsistent confinement contract.
335	- Remediation: route every path argument through `resolve_safe_path` and add the tools to the bridge path check.
336	- Acceptance test: the three calls above return "escapes workspace jail" errors.
337	
338	### T16 search_code/list_dir: no truncation disclosure, unbounded line and entry sizes
339	- Priority: P2
340	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
341	- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
342	- Observed: search_code stops at `max_results` (default 50, search.rs:48-50, :139, :167) and reports
343	  `total_matches: matches.len()` (:191-195), so a capped result is indistinguishable from "exactly 50 matches";
344	  `line_text` is the whole line (:173-177). list_dir and file_tree have no entry cap at all (search.rs:79-115).
345	  Gitignore handling uses the `ignore` crate (`.hidden(true).git_ignore(true)`), which applies .gitignore only inside a
346	  git repository (crate default `require_git`), so in a non-git workspace `node_modules` etc. are walked.
347	  ```
348	  80 lines "needle i" in sub/n.txt: search_code {"query":"needle"} -> "total_matches": 50   (no truncated flag)
349	  one 200 KB minified line containing needleX: search_code output = 200156 bytes for one match
350	  ```
351	  No generic tool-output cap was found in the agent path (grep `MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT|truncateToolOutput|capToolOutput`
352	  over cli/src -> none; `foldVoluminousOutput` applies only to run_command/run_tests, agent.ts:3261-3268).
353	- Remediation: return `truncated: true` and a `scanned_files`/`more_available` hint; clip `line_text` to ~300 chars
354	  around the match with a marker; cap list_dir/file_tree entries with a disclosed limit; set `require_git(false)` so
355	  .gitignore applies in non-git workspaces.
356	- Acceptance test: the two probes return `truncated: true` and output < 10 KB respectively.
357	
358	---
359	
360	## Area 7 — Persistence and auditability
361	
362	Context: durable task state is one JSON file per task (`~/.nexus/tasks/<taskId>.json` via ApplicationCore; sessions dir
363	for SessionManager), `schemaVersion` 1 (core/state.ts:27), saved by temp+rename (state.ts:360-380), loaded fail-closed
364	on corrupt JSON / future versions (state.ts:400-419) with legacy v0 migration (state.ts:810-847). Redaction for
365	persistence is applied on save and re-applied on load (state.ts:335-350, 446-460).
366	
367	### P1 Persistence failures are silently swallowed; the turn reports success-shaped results while nothing is saved
368	- Priority: P1
369	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
370	- Affects: main / feat/tui-surface / fix/context-convergence (same code; convergence only adds `findings`)
371	- Observed: every durable write in the agent loop is wrapped in an empty catch: `persistProgress` (agent.ts:1160-1171),
372	  `recordOperationStart`/`recordOperationEnd` (agent.ts:2583-2593, 2605-2614), milestone recording in update_plan
373	  (agent.ts:2438-2452). Reproduction (mock gateway, test file tp/main/cli/test/zz_probe_persistfail.test.ts: construct
374	  ApplicationCore, chmod the task-state directory 0500, run a turn that writes a.txt and calls task_completed):
375	  ```
376	  PROBE result: {"success":false,"exitCode":2,"outcome":"UNVERIFIED","execution":"COMPLETED","warnings":null}
377	  PROBE a.txt exists: true state bytes before/after: 517 517
378	  PROBE state messages: 0
379	  ```
380	  The workspace changed, the durable record still has 0 messages and no operation record, and neither the TurnResult
381	  nor stderr mentions it (the UNVERIFIED outcome is from missing verification, not from the persistence failure).
382	- Impact: a crash later loses the whole session, interrupted-operation detection (PERS-002) silently stops working, and
383	  `/resume` offers stale state — while the UI implies it is saved.
384	- Remediation: count persistence failures in the agent; surface the first one as a TurnResult warning / TUI banner
385	  ("session is not being saved: <reason>") and in `nexus doctor`; fail the turn closed when `recordOperationStart`
386	  fails for a mutating tool (cannot guarantee interrupted-op detection).
387	- Acceptance test: the probe above yields a turn warning/flag `persistence: "failed"` and a non-zero/explicit exit
388	  reason; TUI shows a banner.
389	
390	### P2 update_plan re-records every completed phase as a new milestone on each call
391	- Priority: P2
392	- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
393	- Affects: all branches
394	- Observed: the update_plan handler loops over all phases and calls `recordMilestone` for each `completed` one
395	  (agent.ts:2435-2452); `recordMilestone` always appends with a fresh `randomUUID()` (state.ts:549-585). Mock-gateway
396	  probe (tp/main/cli/test/zz_probe_milestones.test.ts: three update_plan calls, Research completed in all three,
397	  Implement completed in calls 2-3):
398	  ```
399	  PROBE milestones: ["Research#0","Research#0","Implement#1","Research#0","Implement#1"]
400	  ```
401	- Impact: the milestone ledger (exported verbatim via `...session` in session_export.ts:75-77) overstates progress and
402	  timestamps mean "plan re-sent", not "reached"; any consumer counting milestones is wrong.
403	- Remediation: record a milestone only on a status transition (previous plan phase not completed -> completed), keyed by
404	  (phaseIndex, name); make `recordMilestone` idempotent on that key.
405	- Acceptance test: the probe yields `["Research#0","Implement#1"]`.
406	
407	### P3 Durable state is written without fsync, with default file mode, and without a writer lock
408	- Priority: P2
409	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK (fsync, lock) / REPRODUCED (mode)
410	- Observed:
411	  - `fs.writeFileSync(tempPath, …)` then `fs.renameSync` (state.ts:369-372): no `fsync` of the temp file or directory.
412	    The comment says "synchronous flush"; writeFileSync does not fsync. On power loss the rename can survive with
413	    empty/old data on some filesystems.
414	  - No `mode` is passed: the probe's state file was `664` (`PROBE mode: 664`), whereas the sidecar's diff files and the
415	    compaction archive are written 0600 (sidecar.ts keepOperationDiff on main; session.ts appendArchivedHistory).
416	    The state file holds the (redacted) conversation, tool outputs and objective.
417	  - No lock: two processes resuming the same session (`/resume`, `nexus --resume`, a TUI and a REPL) each do
418	    load-modify-save (state.ts:490-540); last writer wins silently. grep for `lockfile|acquireLock|withLock|flock` in
419	    cli/src finds only doctor.ts.
420	  - Each tool call rewrites the whole file three times (start, end, progress), each with a full parse + redaction pass
421	    (state.ts:481-540) — cost grows with conversation size.
422	- Remediation: open temp with mode 0600, `fsync` file then directory before/after rename; take an advisory lock file
423	  (pid+boot id, as operation_runner.ts:337-360 already does for operations) for the lifetime of a session writer and
424	  refuse/attach read-only on contention; append operation start/end to a small per-session journal instead of
425	  rewriting the whole record.
426	- Acceptance test: state file mode is 0600; a second `ApplicationCore` resuming the same task gets a "session is open in
427	  pid N" error; strace shows fsync on save.
428	
429	### P4 Single-slot `currentOperation` cannot represent parallel calls; crash during a parallel batch under-reports
430	- Priority: P3
431	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
432	- Observed: `recordOperationStart` overwrites the single `currentOperation` (state.ts:481-504). The parallel path
433	  starts several calls at once (agent.ts:3189-3194) — including `run_tests`, which executes repository code (T11). After
434	  the first call ends, `recordOperationEnd` matches by `seq` (state.ts:515-520), so only the last-started call is
435	  tracked. A crash while an earlier-started `run_tests` is still running is recovered without naming it.
436	- Remediation: `inFlightOperations: Record<invocationId, …>`; recovery marks every entry interrupted.
437	- Acceptance test: state test starting two operations then recovering reports both as interrupted.
438	
439	### P5 Session lookup by substring and catch-all null hide which session is resumed and why a load failed
440	- Priority: P3
441	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
442	- Observed: `loadSession`/`recoverSession` fall back to the first session (most recent mtime) whose id *contains* the
443	  argument (session.ts:114, :141); `loadSession` converts every error — corrupt JSON, unsupported schema, workspace
444	  mismatch, redaction failure — into `null` (session.ts:126-128), i.e. "not found". The typed errors from
445	  `loadTaskState` (CorruptStateError, UnsupportedSchemaVersionError, …; state.ts:400-419) are lost at this boundary.
446	- Remediation: exact or unique-prefix match only (error listing candidates when ambiguous); return a typed result
447	  (`not_found | corrupt | unsupported_version | workspace_mismatch`) and print it.
448	- Acceptance test: two sessions `…_ab12` and `…_cd12`, `resume 12` -> ambiguity error; a session file with
449	  `schemaVersion: 2` -> "unsupported schema version 2" rather than "not found".
450	
451	### P6 Cross-branch schema drift without a version bump; older builds drop new fields on save
452	- Priority: P3
453	- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
454	- Affects: fix/context-convergence vs main / installed runtime
455	- Observed: fix/context-convergence adds `findings?: string[]` to DurableTaskState and SessionManager.saveSession
456	  (`git diff main fix/context-convergence -- cli/src/core/state.ts cli/src/session.ts`) with `schemaVersion` still 1.
457	  `saveSession` builds the record from an explicit field list (session.ts:70-98 on main), so a main/feat build that
458	  loads and re-saves a convergence-written session drops `findings` silently. The same branch removes
459	  `SessionManager.operationDiffPath` (and the sidecar's on-disk full-diff copies, sidecar.ts:567-580 on main), so the
460	  complete-diff audit artifact exists on main/feat but not on fix/context-convergence.
461	- Remediation: bump `schemaVersion` when adding durable fields, or preserve unknown top-level fields on save; decide
462	  explicitly whether full diffs are kept and carry that decision into the merge.
463	- Acceptance test: load+save a record with an unknown top-level field preserves it byte-for-byte in that field.
464	
465	### Note on verifier staleness (requested check) — mostly solid
466	A verifier PASS is reused only if candidate identity (tracked + untracked non-ignored files), process epoch,
467	`mutationSeq` and an ignored-inputs fingerprint (PATH, lockfile markers, .env mtimes) all match
468	(objective.ts:410-432, agent.ts:1470-1490, 425-455); every mutating capability bumps `mutationSeq` and demotes
469	`verified` requirements (agent.ts:744-753). Gaps: `run_tests` is non-mutating (T11), so a test run that rewrites
470	snapshots does not invalidate; subagent edits do not demote already-verified requirements (T14); an attempt is recorded
471	PASSED from the filtered/injected command string (T11). Existing tests: cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts covers
472	priorAttempt / SKIPPED_UNCHANGED_INPUTS.
473	
474	---
475	
476	## What is solid (with evidence)
477	- Process-group timeout cleanup: `process_group(0)` + killpg TERM -> 500 ms -> KILL (runner.rs:158, 226-246). Verified:
478	  a TERM-ignoring grandchild is gone after a 2 s timeout; PTY-mode timeout left no survivor.
479	- run_command output truncation keeps head and tail with an explicit `[TRUNCATED n BYTES]` marker (runner.rs:41-53),
480	  apart from the UTF-8 bug (T8). `timed_out` and `duration_ms` are reported; the bridge deadline is derived from the
481	  runner deadline + 5 s grace so the runner's structured result wins (tools.ts:104-120).
482	- cwd confinement for run_command (canonicalised, must be under the workspace; runner.rs:107-126) and descriptor-level
483	  confinement for file reads/writes including a symlink-race test (file_ops.rs:57-86, tests at :1107, :1239, :1291).
484	- patch_file is all-or-nothing in memory: any unmatched hunk returns before touching the file (file_ops.rs:1043-1047).
485	- Pre-flight syntax validation rejects JSON/brace-breaking writes and edits before writing (file_ops.rs:188-203, 568-584).
486	- Per-operation diffs (file_diff.ts) diff the operation's own before/after snapshot, not `git diff`, handle missing
487	  final newline like git (`NO_EOL` sentinel), cap large/binary files with an explicit note, and neutralise terminal
488	  control characters (`visibleControls`).
489	- Durable state: temp+rename, fail-closed load on corrupt JSON and future schema versions, legacy v0 migration,
490	  identity binding to task and workspace, interrupted in-flight operation detection on recovery, offline candidate
491	  mutation invalidates validation receipts — all covered by cli/test/state.test.ts (PERS-001..004, "Corrupt state and
492	  unsupported schema fail closed", "Restart idempotence", "SessionManager migration").
493	- Durable redaction keeps audit identifiers: probe through `redactForPersistence` left a 40-hex git SHA, a sha256, a
494	  UUID and a candidate id intact while redacting a base64 blob; long provider tool-call ids are mapped to stable
495	  `call_<sha256[:12]>` (persistence_protection.ts:28-31; probe: `call_ecf037f30284`) so call/result pairing survives.
496	- Export `nexus-session-export/2` states explicitly whether the history is complete or compacted and includes archived
497	  originals when present (session_export.ts:29-58).
498	- RPC daemon runs requests concurrently (`tokio::spawn` + `spawn_blocking`, main.rs:194-222) and converts a panicking
499	  tool into an error response instead of dying.
500	
501	## Checks actually run
502	| Command / probe | Result |
503	|---|---|
504	| `git archive 3727938` -> tp/main; `cargo build --release` (RUSTUP_HOME/CARGO_HOME of the user, HOME temp) | built, exit 0 |

511	| run_command 12000 x '€' | engine panic runner.rs:47 (T8) |
512	| rpc.py: run_command `timeout 3 cat > stolen.txt` + list_dir + write_file | write_file request found in stolen.txt, never answered, x.txt absent (T6) |
513	| run_command `(sleep 8; echo late) & echo early`, timeout 3 | wall 8.03 s, timed_out false (T7) |
514	| run_command TERM-ignoring grandchild, timeout 2; PTY variant | no survivors (solid) |

517	| tsx probe_runtests.mts (filter injection) | INJECTED_BY_FILTER created, success true (T11) |

# Nexus Code — Tool/Execution Quality (Area 3) and Persistence/Auditability (Area 7)

STATUS: COMPLETE (2026-10-12). Findings T1-T16 (Area 3) and P1-P6 (Area 7).

Scope and method: independent, read-only review. Primary commit main 3727938, extracted with `git archive` to
`scratchpad/assess/tp/main` (engine built there with `cargo build --release`; node_modules symlinked). All probes ran
in throwaway workspaces under `scratchpad/assess/tp/ws*` with `HOME=scratchpad/assess/tp/home`. Below, `HC` =
`tp/main/core/target/release/harness-core`.

Branch applicability: `git diff --stat main feat/tui-surface` and `main fix/context-convergence` show **no changes** to
`core/src/file_ops.rs`, `core/src/runner.rs`, `core/src/main.rs`, `cli/src/tools.ts`, `cli/src/sandbox.ts`,
`cli/src/tester.ts`, `cli/src/file_diff.ts`'s callers in the tool path. fix/context-convergence changes only
`cli/src/core/state.ts` (+4) and `cli/src/session.ts` (+1/-8) among the persistence files. So every Area 3 finding
applies to main, feat/tui-surface, fix/context-convergence, and the installed runtime (which runs the
feat/tui-surface checkout).

## Area 3 — Tool and execution quality

### T1 edit_file silently applies to non-matching text (fuzzy 0.85 fallback) and deletes code the model never named
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: main / feat/tui-surface / fix/context-convergence / installed runtime
- Trigger: `edit_file` whose `old_content` is not in the file (e.g. stale model view), but a same-sized window is
  >= 85% line-similar.
- Expected: the edit is refused ("old_content not found"), or at minimum the result discloses that a fuzzy match
  replaced different text.
- Observed: main core/src/file_ops.rs:243-322 (`fuzzy_find_and_replace`, threshold `best_ratio = 0.85f32` at :299)
  is the fourth fallback in `edit_file` (:558-560). It replaces the most similar window and returns
  `replacements: 1` with no indication that a fuzzy match occurred. Reproduction:
  ```
  printf 'fn f() {\n    let a = 1;\n    let b = 2;\n    audit_log(a);\n    let c = 3;\n    let d = 4;\n    let e = 5;\n    let g = 6;\n}\n' > f.rs
  $HC -w . call --tool edit_file --args '{"path":"f.rs","old_content":"    let a = 1;\n    let b = 2;\n    check_permissions(a);\n    let c = 3;\n    let d = 4;\n    let e = 5;\n    let g = 6;","new_content":"    let a = 1;\n    let b = 2;\n    let c = 3;\n    let d = 4;\n    let e = 5;\n    let g = 7;"}'
  -> exit 0, "replacements": 1, diff "-    audit_log(a);" ... "+    let g = 7;"
  ```
  `check_permissions(a)` never existed; the line `audit_log(a);` was deleted. The only test of this path
  (file_ops.rs:1168, "fuzzy indentation mismatch") covers the benign case.
- Impact: silent semantic corruption of source on a stale or hallucinated snippet; the transcript and receipt say
  the edit succeeded as asked.
- Remediation: remove the TextDiff-ratio fallback (keep exact, CRLF-normalised and per-line-trim matching); if any
  non-exact strategy matched, return `match: "exact"|"newline_normalized"|"trimmed_lines"` in `EditFileResult` and
  refuse when the matched region's text differs from `old_content` beyond whitespace.
- Acceptance test: Rust unit test with the file above asserts `edit_file` returns `Err` and the file is byte-identical.
- Dependencies: none. Not addressed on any branch.

### T2 edit_file replaces the first of several matches and reports the total as `replacements`
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Trigger: `old_content` occurs more than once.
- Expected: refusal for ambiguity (model must add context), or replace all and say so.
- Observed: file_ops.rs:540-543 — `count = matches().count()` but `replacen(.., 1)`; same at :551-552 and :557-558.
  ```
  printf 'a = 1\nb = 2\na = 1\n' > dup.txt
  $HC -w . call --tool edit_file --args '{"path":"dup.txt","old_content":"a = 1","new_content":"a = 9"}'
  -> "replacements": 2 ; file afterwards: "a = 9\nb = 2\na = 1"
  ```
  The tool description (capabilities.ts:265-297) says "Exact snippet"; the system prompt asks for "unique snippets"
  (agent.ts:1968) but nothing enforces it. `flight.ts:191-195` records `replacements` from the *args* (always
  undefined -> 1), not from the result.
- Impact: wrong occurrence edited; result claims two replacements when one happened — misleading receipts.
- Remediation: when count > 1 return `Err("old_content matches N locations; include more context")`; add optional
  `replace_all: bool`. Report the number actually replaced.
- Acceptance test: unit test above expects `Err` and unchanged file; with `replace_all:true` expects 2 replacements.

### T3 edit_file / write_file are non-atomic, have no stale-content guard, and edit_file can rewrite line endings
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT (CRLF rewrite; status field) / SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK (atomicity, staleness)
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed:
  - In-place truncate-then-write, no temp file, no fsync: write_file file_ops.rs:213-225 (`set_len(0)` at :223),
    edit_file :600-609 (`set_len(0)` at :607). A crash, kill, ENOSPC or EIO after `set_len(0)` leaves an empty or
    partial file; the error path returns `Failed to write...` but the original is already gone. Because the receipt
    is unsuccessful, the per-operation diff is not recorded either (agent.ts:2638 requires `receipt.success`).
  - No stale-content detection: edit_file reads the file at call time (:530-537) and there is no expected-hash /
    mtime parameter anywhere (grep for `expected_hash|mtime|stale|lastRead` over core/src/file_ops.rs, cli/src/agent.ts,
    cli/src/file_diff.ts finds only the verifier fingerprint). Combined with T1, an operator edit made between the
    model's read and its edit can be overwritten by a fuzzy match.
  - CRLF rewrite: when the exact match fails, the newline-normalised fallback returns the whole file normalised
    (:545-552), converting every CRLF in the file to LF:
    ```
    printf 'line1\r\nline2\r\nline3\r\n' > crlf.txt
    $HC -w . call --tool edit_file --args '{"path":"crlf.txt","old_content":"line1\nline2","new_content":"LINE1\nline2"}'
    od -c crlf.txt -> "L I N E 1 \n l i n e 2 \n l i n e 3 \n"   (all \r removed)
    ```
  - Non-UTF-8 files: `read_to_string` (:535) fails, so Latin-1 files cannot be edited at all (fails closed; acceptable).
  - write_file always reports `"status": "overwritten"`, even for a new file, because it tests `target.exists()`
    after writing (:231). Reproduced: `write_file brand_new.txt` -> `"status": "overwritten"`.
- Impact: data loss on interruption; line-ending churn producing whole-file diffs in Windows-authored repos;
  misleading created/overwritten audit status.
- Remediation: write to a sibling temp created with `tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(parent)`, copy the original's
  permissions, `sync_all`, `persist` (rename), fsync parent dir; detect the file's dominant EOL and BOM and
  re-apply them to `new_content`; compute status before writing; add optional `expected_sha256` to edit/patch/write
  and have the agent pass the hash of the content it last read.
- Acceptance test: (a) CRLF file edited with LF snippet keeps `\r\n` on every line; (b) `write_file` new path ->
  `created`; (c) fault-injection test (write to a file on a full tmpfs or a read-only bind of the temp dir) leaves the
  original byte-identical; (d) edit with wrong `expected_sha256` -> `Err`, file unchanged.

### T4 patch_file clobbers `<stem>.tmp_patch`, drops the executable bit, replaces symlinks, strips CRLF, ignores hunk line numbers
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: patch_file (file_ops.rs:943-1088) is all-or-nothing in memory (returns before writing if any hunk fails,
  :1043-1047 — good) and commits by rename, but:
  - temp path is `target.with_extension("tmp_patch")` (:1054), a fixed, predictable sibling: an existing
    `run.tmp_patch` is truncated, overwritten and renamed away.
  - the temp is created with default mode and renamed over the target (:1056-1069): permissions are not preserved.
  - rename replaces a symlink with a regular file; the link target is left unpatched.
  - `original_content.lines()` (:1017) strips `\r`; the file is re-joined with `\n`.
  - `@@` headers are discarded (:974-984); each hunk applies at the **first** matching context anywhere in the file
    (:1030-1036), so a hunk aimed at the second of two identical blocks patches the first.
  ```
  printf '#!/bin/sh\necho old\n' > run.sh; chmod 755 run.sh; printf 'IMPORTANT USER DATA\n' > run.tmp_patch
  $HC -w . call --tool patch_file --args '{"path":"run.sh","patch":"@@ -1,2 +1,2 @@\n #!/bin/sh\n-echo old\n+echo new\n"}'
  ls -l -> "-rw-rw-r-- run.sh" (was -rwxr-xr-x); run.tmp_patch: No such file or directory
  printf 'x\ny\n' > real.txt; ln -s real.txt link.txt
  $HC ... patch_file link.txt "-x\n+X\n y\n" -> link.txt is now a regular file; real.txt still "x\ny"
  printf 'a\r\nb\r\n' > c.txt; patch "-a\n+A\n" -> diff "-a\r\n-b\r\n+A\n+b\n"; od: "A \n b \n"
  ```
- Impact: user data destroyed; scripts stop being executable; symlinked config silently forked; whole-file EOL churn;
  misplaced hunks.
- Remediation: random temp name in the same dir (NamedTempFile), copy metadata (mode) from the original, resolve the
  symlink and patch the real path (after confinement check), preserve EOL, honour `@@ -l` as the search start and
  require a unique match (or the nearest to the stated line).
- Acceptance test: the four commands above produce: run.tmp_patch intact, run.sh mode 755, real.txt patched with
  link.txt still a symlink, c.txt keeps CRLF; plus a two-identical-blocks fixture where `@@ -10` patches the second.

### T5 delete_file recursively removes directories without an approval gate and records no detail
- Priority: P2
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: `delete_file` on a directory calls `fs::remove_dir_all` (file_ops.rs:640-641). The agent's approval
  prompt covers only `edit_file|write_file|patch_file|run_command` (agent.ts:2503-2508); `delete_file` is not in that
  list. The per-op diff snapshot treats a directory as `unreadable: not a regular file` (file_diff.ts:31-34), so the
  change is recorded as one "deleted" entry with no file list. The name and description suggest a file.
- Impact: one model call can delete a whole subtree (e.g. `src`) with no prompt in review mode and no record of what
  was removed.
- Remediation: refuse directories unless `recursive: true`; include `delete_file` in the approval set; record the
  list of removed paths (and sizes) in the receipt; snapshot-to-checkpoint before deleting.
- Acceptance test: agent test with an onConfirm that denies: `delete_file {path:"src"}` is DENIED and `src` exists;
  engine test: directory without `recursive` -> Err.

### T6 run_command child inherits the RPC daemon's stdin and consumes queued tool requests
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Trigger: any command that reads stdin (`cat`, `read`, `head`, prompts from `npm init`, `apt`, `git` credential
  prompts, `python` REPL...) while another RPC request is sent to the same daemon (parallel read-only tools, MCP,
  sub-agents sharing the bridge, a retried/timed-out request).
- Expected: commands get `/dev/null` (or a closed pipe) as stdin; requests are never lost.
- Observed: runner.rs:151-153 sets stdout/stderr only; `Command` defaults stdin to *inherit*, and in RPC mode fd 0 is
  the JSON-RPC request pipe that the tokio reader also reads (main.rs:185). Reproduction with a 30-line driver
  (`tp/scripts/rpc.py`, sends JSON lines to `harness-core rpc`):
  ```
  python3 -I rpc.py $HC ws2 '[[0,"run_command",{"command":"timeout 3 cat > stolen.txt; echo done","timeout_secs":10}],
                              [0.5,"list_dir",{"path":"."}],[0.5,"write_file",{"path":"x.txt","content":"x"}]]' 5
  [ 0.5s] RESP {"id":2,...list_dir result...}
  [ 3.1s] RESP {"id":1,..."stdout":"done\n","timed_out":false}
  (no response for id 3)
  stolen.txt: {"id": 3, "method": "write_file", "params": {"path": "x.txt", "content": "x"}}
  ls x.txt -> No such file or directory
  ```
  A first run with `head -c 60` similarly swallowed request 3 (`list_dir`), which never got a reply. The bridge then
  reports `RPC request ... timed out ... (result unknown)` after 35 s (tools.ts:324-335). Interactive commands also hang
  for the whole timeout instead of failing at EOF.
- Impact: lost tool calls, spurious 35 s stalls with "result unknown", interactive prompts hanging to timeout.
- Remediation: `cmd.stdin(Stdio::null())` in `run_command` (runner.rs) and in the PTY path; keep the RPC pipe private
  (dup fd 0 to a high fd at daemon start and reopen 0 as /dev/null).
- Acceptance test: the rpc.py scenario above returns responses for ids 1-3, `x.txt` exists, `stolen.txt` is empty;
  `run_command {"command":"read x; echo rc=$?"}` returns immediately with `rc=1`.

### T7 run_command timeout does not bound the call once the shell exits; background children hold it open
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: the deadline loop (runner.rs:184-199) only watches the shell. After the shell exits, the reader threads
  are joined unconditionally (:202-203) and block until every descendant holding the pipes exits; the process group is
  not killed on normal exit.
  ```
  /usr/bin/time $HC -w . call --tool run_command --args '{"command":"(sleep 8; echo late) & echo early","timeout_secs":3}'
  -> "stdout": "early\nlate\n", "timed_out": false, "exit_code": 0, wall=8.03s
  ```
  With a server started in the background (`npm run dev &`) the call never returns; the bridge gives up after
  `timeout_secs + 5` with "result unknown" (tools.ts:113-120) while the daemon thread and the server live on.
- Solid by contrast: on a real timeout the whole group is SIGTERM'd then SIGKILL'd (runner.rs:226-246). Verified: a
  SIGTERM-ignoring grandchild (`exec -a nxprobeign sleep 300` with `trap "" TERM`) is gone 1 s after a 2 s timeout
  (`pgrep -x nxprobeign` -> none); PTY-mode timeout also left no survivor. `setsid -f` children escape (expected).
- Remediation: apply the deadline to the pipe drain too (read with a deadline, or after shell exit wait at most a short
  grace then `killpg` and mark `background_children_killed`); document/offer a `background: true` mode that redirects
  output to a log file and returns a handle.
- Acceptance test: the command above returns within `timeout_secs + 1` s with `timed_out: true` (or a
  `children_killed` flag) and no `sleep 8` survives.

### T8 run_command panics on large multi-byte output; result (and exit code) are lost after the side effects ran
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: `truncate_output` slices `&s[..half]` / `&s[s.len()-half..]` at byte offsets (runner.rs:42-53); any output
  > 32 000 bytes whose byte 16 000 is inside a UTF-8 character panics.
  ```
  $HC -w . call --tool run_command --args '{"command":"python3 -c \"print(chr(8364)*12000)\"","timeout_secs":10}'
  thread 'main' panicked at src/runner.rs:47:15: end byte index 16000 is not a char boundary; it is inside '€'
  ```
  In RPC mode the panic is caught by `spawn_blocking` and returned as `Task execution failed` (main.rs:200-222), so
  the agent sees a failed command although it ran to completion (e.g. a migration or `git commit`). Panic text goes to
  the daemon's stderr, which the bridge pipes but never reads (tools.ts:209-212, no stderr listener): enough panics
  would fill the pipe and block the daemon.
- Remediation: truncate on char boundaries (`s.floor_char_boundary`, or truncate the byte buffer before lossy
  decoding); drain or `ignore` daemon stderr in the bridge.
- Acceptance test: the command above returns success with a `[TRUNCATED N BYTES]` marker; unit test with 3-byte chars.

### T9 run_command buffers unbounded output in memory before truncating
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Observed: reader threads `read_to_end` into a `Vec` with no cap (runner.rs:166-178); truncation to 32 000 chars
  happens only at the end (:208-214). A noisy command (`yes`, verbose build) for 60 s can allocate GBs in the engine.
  The truncation marker itself is good (`... [TRUNCATED n BYTES] ...`, head+tail kept).
- Remediation: ring-buffer head (16 KB) + tail (16 KB) while streaming, counting dropped bytes.
- Acceptance test: `yes | head -c 2000000000` keeps engine RSS < 100 MB and reports the dropped byte count.

### T10 Commands inherit the full environment; arbitrary-format secrets reach the model provider
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: no `env_clear`/`env_remove` in core/src or cli/src (grep `env_clear|env_remove|clearenv` -> none); the
  bridge spawns the daemon with the sidecar's env (tools.ts:209-212) and the runner passes it on; bwrap wrapping also
  keeps the env (sandbox.ts, no `--clearenv`).
  ```
  REDACTED REDACTED \
    $HC -w . call --tool run_command --args '{"command":"env | grep -E \"API_KEY\"","timeout_secs":5}'
  -> "stdout": "OPENAI_API_KEY=REDACTED real key from the reviewer's shell, redacted here>\nREDACTED
  ```
  The egress boundary tokenises only pattern-matched secrets before the provider call. Probe through
  `InformationFlowBoundary.evaluateEgress` (tp/main/cli/probe_egress.mts):
  `OPENAI_API_KEY=REDACTED but `REDACTED and
  `DATABASE_URL=REDACTED` pass through unchanged (quarantinedCount 1).
- Impact: the operator's gateway key (`LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, used by Nexus itself), DB URLs and other unquoted env
  secrets are one `env`/`printenv` away from the transcript, the provider and the session file.
- Remediation: build the child env from an allow-list (PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, USER, SHELL, TMPDIR, project-declared
  vars) and strip Nexus's own credential vars (`LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY`, `*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`) unless the operator opts in;
  also tokenise values of env vars whose names match `KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD` in tool output.
- Acceptance test: with `LOCAL_LLM_API_KEY=REDACTED set, `run_command env` output does not contain `x123456789`.

### T11 run_tests: filter is shell-injected, executes without approval, and is scheduled as a parallel "read-only" tool
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: `detectTestCommand` interpolates the model-supplied `filter` into a shell string — unquoted for Cargo
  (`cargo test -- ${filterPattern}`, tester.ts:37) and inside naive double quotes for make/npm/pytest/go (:30, :47, :55,
  :60). `run_tests` calls `this.executeTool("run_command", …)` directly (tools.ts:556-561), bypassing the agent's
  approval prompt, which never includes `run_tests` (agent.ts:2503-2508). `run_tests` is also in `READ_ONLY_TOOLS`
  (agent.ts:378-389) and capabilities marks it `mutating: false` (capabilities.ts:788-790), so it runs concurrently with
  other tools via `Promise.all` (agent.ts:3186-3194) and does not bump `mutationSeq` (agent.ts:744-749).
  ```
  ws3/package.json: {"scripts":{"test":"echo tests-ran"}}
  tsx probe_runtests.mts ws3   (RustCoreBridge(ws3).executeTool("run_tests", {filter: 'x" ; touch INJECTED_BY_FILTER ; echo "'}))
  command: npm test -- -t "x" ; touch INJECTED_BY_FILTER ; echo ""
  success: true
  ls ws3 -> INJECTED_BY_FILTER  package.json
  ```
  The trailing `echo ""` also makes the exit status 0, so a failing suite can be recorded as a PASSED verifier
  attempt (agent.ts:2623-2634 records status from `parsed.passed && receipt.success`).
- Impact: approval bypass for arbitrary shell; forged verifier passes; test runs that write files racing with
  parallel reads, unnoticed by staleness tracking.
- Remediation: pass the filter as an argv element (no shell) or reject anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_:./ -]`; treat
  run_tests as mutating/proc (remove from READ_ONLY_TOOLS; bump mutationSeq); route it through the same approval policy
  as run_command; record verifier attempts only for the configured, unfiltered command.
- Acceptance test: the probe above leaves no `INJECTED_BY_FILTER` and returns an argument-validation error; agent test
  shows `run_tests` + `read_file` in one response are executed sequentially.

### T12 Parallel read-only path skips the cancellation check and output folding
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Observed: the sequential path checks `signal.aborted` before each dispatch (agent.ts:3225-3235) and folds voluminous
  run_command/run_tests output (:3261-3268); the parallel path (:3186-3218) does neither, so a cancelled turn still
  dispatches every parallel call and an unfolded `run_tests` result goes to context. The RPC daemon has no cancel verb
  (acknowledged in agent.ts:2707), so in-flight commands always run to their own timeout after cancel.
- Remediation: check `signal.aborted` before `Promise.all`; apply `foldVoluminousOutput` identically; add a `cancel`
  RPC that `killpg`s the request's process group.
- Acceptance test: cancel during a 2-call parallel batch -> both calls get `cancelledToolMessage`; cancel during
  `run_command sleep 30` returns within 1 s and no `sleep` survives.

### T14 spawn_subagent: "isolated" helper shares the workspace and its tool calls skip the approval prompt
- Priority: P1
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime (REPL review mode and TUI approvals)
- Observed: without an active worktree the subagent config is `{...this.config}` with the same workspace
  (agent.ts:2195-2210) although the spinner says "Spawning isolated subagent". `runSubagent` dispatches every call as
  `dispatchToolCall(call, currentStep, "subagent")` with no `onConfirm` (agent.ts:3648), and the approval gate only runs
  when `onConfirm` is passed (agent.ts:2502-2508). So in review mode (`autoApprove=false`, repl.ts:282) or with TUI
  approvals (sidecar.ts:391-421), the parent's `spawn_subagent` call is not prompted (not in the gate list) and the
  child's `write_file`/`edit_file`/`run_command` run unprompted. Child edits also do not bump the parent's
  `mutationSeq` or call `invalidateVerified` (only `turnMutations`/`unverifiedChanges` are propagated, agent.ts:2238-2246),
  so a requirement already marked `verified` keeps that status in the ledger (and export) after a child edits the
  deliverable; a *new* verification is still blocked because the candidate identity changes (agent.ts:1480-1490).
- Impact: approval policy bypass by delegation; ledger shows "verified" for a changed deliverable until a later parent
  mutation demotes it.
- Remediation: pass the parent's `onConfirm` to the child (or force the child read-only unless a worktree is
  bound); include `spawn_subagent` in the approval gate; on child mutations call `invalidateVerified` and bump
  `mutationSeq` in the parent's `finally`.
- Acceptance test: mock-gateway agent test (pattern of cli/test/context_capacity_runtask.test.ts): parent calls
  `spawn_subagent`, child calls `write_file`; with an `onConfirm` that denies, the file is absent; with a requirement
  previously `verified`, after the child write its status is `implemented`.

- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: these use `base_dir.join(&args.path)` (core/src/search.rs:67 list_dir, :387 file_tree; core/src/cst.rs:146)

### T16 search_code/list_dir: no truncation disclosure, unbounded line and entry sizes
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches / installed runtime
- Observed: search_code stops at `max_results` (default 50, search.rs:48-50, :139, :167) and reports
  `total_matches: matches.len()` (:191-195), so a capped result is indistinguishable from "exactly 50 matches";
  `line_text` is the whole line (:173-177). list_dir and file_tree have no entry cap at all (search.rs:79-115).
  Gitignore handling uses the `ignore` crate (`.hidden(true).git_ignore(true)`), which applies .gitignore only inside a
  git repository (crate default `require_git`), so in a non-git workspace `node_modules` etc. are walked.
  ```
  80 lines "needle i" in sub/n.txt: search_code {"query":"needle"} -> "total_matches": 50   (no truncated flag)
  one 200 KB minified line containing needleX: search_code output = 200156 bytes for one match
  ```
  No generic tool-output cap was found in the agent path (grep `MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT|truncateToolOutput|capToolOutput`
  over cli/src -> none; `foldVoluminousOutput` applies only to run_command/run_tests, agent.ts:3261-3268).
- Remediation: return `truncated: true` and a `scanned_files`/`more_available` hint; clip `line_text` to ~300 chars
  around the match with a marker; cap list_dir/file_tree entries with a disclosed limit; set `require_git(false)` so
  .gitignore applies in non-git workspaces.
- Acceptance test: the two probes return `truncated: true` and output < 10 KB respectively.

---

## Area 7 — Persistence and auditability

Context: durable task state is one JSON file per task (`~/.nexus/tasks/<taskId>.json` via ApplicationCore; sessions dir
for SessionManager), `schemaVersion` 1 (core/state.ts:27), saved by temp+rename (state.ts:360-380), loaded fail-closed
on corrupt JSON / future versions (state.ts:400-419) with legacy v0 migration (state.ts:810-847). Redaction for
persistence is applied on save and re-applied on load (state.ts:335-350, 446-460).

### P1 Persistence failures are silently swallowed; the turn reports success-shaped results while nothing is saved
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: main / feat/tui-surface / fix/context-convergence (same code; convergence only adds `findings`)
- Observed: every durable write in the agent loop is wrapped in an empty catch: `persistProgress` (agent.ts:1160-1171),
  `recordOperationStart`/`recordOperationEnd` (agent.ts:2583-2593, 2605-2614), milestone recording in update_plan
  (agent.ts:2438-2452). Reproduction (mock gateway, test file tp/main/cli/test/zz_probe_persistfail.test.ts: construct
  ApplicationCore, chmod the task-state directory 0500, run a turn that writes a.txt and calls task_completed):
  ```
  PROBE result: {"success":false,"exitCode":2,"outcome":"UNVERIFIED","execution":"COMPLETED","warnings":null}
  PROBE a.txt exists: true state bytes before/after: 517 517
  PROBE state messages: 0
  ```
  The workspace changed, the durable record still has 0 messages and no operation record, and neither the TurnResult
  nor stderr mentions it (the UNVERIFIED outcome is from missing verification, not from the persistence failure).
- Impact: a crash later loses the whole session, interrupted-operation detection (PERS-002) silently stops working, and
  `/resume` offers stale state — while the UI implies it is saved.
- Remediation: count persistence failures in the agent; surface the first one as a TurnResult warning / TUI banner
  ("session is not being saved: <reason>") and in `nexus doctor`; fail the turn closed when `recordOperationStart`
  fails for a mutating tool (cannot guarantee interrupted-op detection).
- Acceptance test: the probe above yields a turn warning/flag `persistence: "failed"` and a non-zero/explicit exit
  reason; TUI shows a banner.

### P2 update_plan re-records every completed phase as a new milestone on each call
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all branches
- Observed: the update_plan handler loops over all phases and calls `recordMilestone` for each `completed` one
  (agent.ts:2435-2452); `recordMilestone` always appends with a fresh `randomUUID()` (state.ts:549-585). Mock-gateway
  probe (tp/main/cli/test/zz_probe_milestones.test.ts: three update_plan calls, Research completed in all three,
  Implement completed in calls 2-3):
  ```
  PROBE milestones: ["Research#0","Research#0","Implement#1","Research#0","Implement#1"]
  ```
- Impact: the milestone ledger (exported verbatim via `...session` in session_export.ts:75-77) overstates progress and
  timestamps mean "plan re-sent", not "reached"; any consumer counting milestones is wrong.
- Remediation: record a milestone only on a status transition (previous plan phase not completed -> completed), keyed by
  (phaseIndex, name); make `recordMilestone` idempotent on that key.
- Acceptance test: the probe yields `["Research#0","Implement#1"]`.

### P3 Durable state is written without fsync, with default file mode, and without a writer lock
- Priority: P2
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK (fsync, lock) / REPRODUCED (mode)
- Observed:
  - `fs.writeFileSync(tempPath, …)` then `fs.renameSync` (state.ts:369-372): no `fsync` of the temp file or directory.
    The comment says "synchronous flush"; writeFileSync does not fsync. On power loss the rename can survive with
    empty/old data on some filesystems.
  - No `mode` is passed: the probe's state file was `664` (`PROBE mode: 664`), whereas the sidecar's diff files and the
    compaction archive are written 0600 (sidecar.ts keepOperationDiff on main; session.ts appendArchivedHistory).
    The state file holds the (redacted) conversation, tool outputs and objective.
  - No lock: two processes resuming the same session (`/resume`, `nexus --resume`, a TUI and a REPL) each do
    load-modify-save (state.ts:490-540); last writer wins silently. grep for `lockfile|acquireLock|withLock|flock` in
    cli/src finds only doctor.ts.
  - Each tool call rewrites the whole file three times (start, end, progress), each with a full parse + redaction pass
    (state.ts:481-540) — cost grows with conversation size.
- Remediation: open temp with mode 0600, `fsync` file then directory before/after rename; take an advisory lock file
  (pid+boot id, as operation_runner.ts:337-360 already does for operations) for the lifetime of a session writer and
  refuse/attach read-only on contention; append operation start/end to a small per-session journal instead of
  rewriting the whole record.
- Acceptance test: state file mode is 0600; a second `ApplicationCore` resuming the same task gets a "session is open in
  pid N" error; strace shows fsync on save.

### P4 Single-slot `currentOperation` cannot represent parallel calls; crash during a parallel batch under-reports
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Observed: `recordOperationStart` overwrites the single `currentOperation` (state.ts:481-504). The parallel path
  starts several calls at once (agent.ts:3189-3194) — including `run_tests`, which executes repository code (T11). After
  the first call ends, `recordOperationEnd` matches by `seq` (state.ts:515-520), so only the last-started call is
  tracked. A crash while an earlier-started `run_tests` is still running is recovered without naming it.
- Remediation: `inFlightOperations: Record<invocationId, …>`; recovery marks every entry interrupted.
- Acceptance test: state test starting two operations then recovering reports both as interrupted.

### P5 Session lookup by substring and catch-all null hide which session is resumed and why a load failed
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Observed: `loadSession`/`recoverSession` fall back to the first session (most recent mtime) whose id *contains* the
  argument (session.ts:114, :141); `loadSession` converts every error — corrupt JSON, unsupported schema, workspace
  mismatch, redaction failure — into `null` (session.ts:126-128), i.e. "not found". The typed errors from
  `loadTaskState` (CorruptStateError, UnsupportedSchemaVersionError, …; state.ts:400-419) are lost at this boundary.
- Remediation: exact or unique-prefix match only (error listing candidates when ambiguous); return a typed result
  (`not_found | corrupt | unsupported_version | workspace_mismatch`) and print it.
- Acceptance test: two sessions `…_ab12` and `…_cd12`, `resume 12` -> ambiguity error; a session file with
  `schemaVersion: 2` -> "unsupported schema version 2" rather than "not found".

### P6 Cross-branch schema drift without a version bump; older builds drop new fields on save
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Affects: fix/context-convergence vs main / installed runtime
- Observed: fix/context-convergence adds `findings?: string[]` to DurableTaskState and SessionManager.saveSession
  (`git diff main fix/context-convergence -- cli/src/core/state.ts cli/src/session.ts`) with `schemaVersion` still 1.
  `saveSession` builds the record from an explicit field list (session.ts:70-98 on main), so a main/feat build that
  loads and re-saves a convergence-written session drops `findings` silently. The same branch removes
  `SessionManager.operationDiffPath` (and the sidecar's on-disk full-diff copies, sidecar.ts:567-580 on main), so the
  complete-diff audit artifact exists on main/feat but not on fix/context-convergence.
- Remediation: bump `schemaVersion` when adding durable fields, or preserve unknown top-level fields on save; decide
  explicitly whether full diffs are kept and carry that decision into the merge.
- Acceptance test: load+save a record with an unknown top-level field preserves it byte-for-byte in that field.

### Note on verifier staleness (requested check) — mostly solid
A verifier PASS is reused only if candidate identity (tracked + untracked non-ignored files), process epoch,
`mutationSeq` and an ignored-inputs fingerprint (PATH, lockfile markers, .env mtimes) all match
(objective.ts:410-432, agent.ts:1470-1490, 425-455); every mutating capability bumps `mutationSeq` and demotes
`verified` requirements (agent.ts:744-753). Gaps: `run_tests` is non-mutating (T11), so a test run that rewrites
snapshots does not invalidate; subagent edits do not demote already-verified requirements (T14); an attempt is recorded
PASSED from the filtered/injected command string (T11). Existing tests: cli/test/objective_continuation.test.ts covers
priorAttempt / SKIPPED_UNCHANGED_INPUTS.

## What is solid (with evidence)
- Process-group timeout cleanup: `process_group(0)` + killpg TERM -> 500 ms -> KILL (runner.rs:158, 226-246). Verified:
  a TERM-ignoring grandchild is gone after a 2 s timeout; PTY-mode timeout left no survivor.
- run_command output truncation keeps head and tail with an explicit `[TRUNCATED n BYTES]` marker (runner.rs:41-53),
  apart from the UTF-8 bug (T8). `timed_out` and `duration_ms` are reported; the bridge deadline is derived from the
  runner deadline + 5 s grace so the runner's structured result wins (tools.ts:104-120).
- cwd confinement for run_command (canonicalised, must be under the workspace; runner.rs:107-126) and descriptor-level
  confinement for file reads/writes including a symlink-race test (file_ops.rs:57-86, tests at :1107, :1239, :1291).
- patch_file is all-or-nothing in memory: any unmatched hunk returns before touching the file (file_ops.rs:1043-1047).
- Pre-flight syntax validation rejects JSON/brace-breaking writes and edits before writing (file_ops.rs:188-203, 568-584).
- Per-operation diffs (file_diff.ts) diff the operation's own before/after snapshot, not `git diff`, handle missing
  final newline like git (`NO_EOL` sentinel), cap large/binary files with an explicit note, and neutralise terminal
  control characters (`visibleControls`).
- Durable state: temp+rename, fail-closed load on corrupt JSON and future schema versions, legacy v0 migration,
  identity binding to task and workspace, interrupted in-flight operation detection on recovery, offline candidate
  mutation invalidates validation receipts — all covered by cli/test/state.test.ts (PERS-001..004, "Corrupt state and
  unsupported schema fail closed", "Restart idempotence", "SessionManager migration").
- Durable redaction keeps audit identifiers: probe through `redactForPersistence` left a 40-hex git SHA, a sha256, a
  UUID and a candidate id intact while redacting a base64 blob; long provider tool-call ids are mapped to stable
  `call_<sha256[:12]>` (persistence_protection.ts:28-31; probe: `call_ecf037f30284`) so call/result pairing survives.
- Export `nexus-session-export/2` states explicitly whether the history is complete or compacted and includes archived
  originals when present (session_export.ts:29-58).
- RPC daemon runs requests concurrently (`tokio::spawn` + `spawn_blocking`, main.rs:194-222) and converts a panicking
  tool into an error response instead of dying.

- Affects: all three branches
- Trigger: model calls `batch_read {paths:[".env"]}` (or `run_command cat .env`, `search_code`/`grep`).
- Expected: `.env` (a DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATH) is not readable by any tool, or its values are redacted before leaving the host.
- Observed: the protected-path check covers `write_file|edit_file|patch_file|delete_file|read_file` only (3727938:cli/src/tools.ts:432-441).
  R6: `read_file` → "Security Policy Violation: Path '.env' is protected", but `batch_read` → `"content": "    1 | REDACTED
  and the second chat request to the gateway contained the secret (`secretSentToModel:true`). The outbound vault patterns
  (security.ts:131-147) do not match an unquoted `KEY=value` line.
- Impact: credentials in `.env` reach whatever endpoint is configured (cloud providers included) despite a policy that claims to protect them.
- Remediation: enforce `isPathProtected` inside the Rust path resolver (`resolve_safe_path`) for every file tool (`batch_read`, `file_info`,
  search/trigram/outline), and filter protected paths out of search/list results; add an unquoted `^[A-Z0-9_]*(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD)[A-Z0-9_]*=.+$` rule to egress redaction.
- Acceptance test: R6 rig → all three calls fail or redact; `gw.requests[1]` does not contain the secret.
- Dependencies: none.

### T-06 `run_tests.filter` is interpolated into a shell command and `run_tests` is not approval-gated: arbitrary command execution in review mode
- Priority: P0
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: main, feat/tui-surface, fix/context-convergence, installed runtime (tester.ts/tools.ts identical)
- Trigger: review mode; model calls `run_tests {filter: 'x" ; touch INJECTED ; echo "'}`.
- Expected: filter passed as a single argv element (or rejected), and running repository test code asks for approval in review mode.
- Observed: `detectTestCommand` builds strings like `npm test -- -t "${filterPattern}"`, `cargo test -- ${filterPattern}` (unquoted), `pytest -k "${filterPattern}"`
  (3727938:cli/src/tester.ts:30,37,47,50,55,60); `run_tests` is `mutating:false` (core/capabilities.ts:787-790) and not in the approval list
  (agent.ts:2502-2508). R9 (review): `approvals:[]`, tool output `"command":"npm test -- -t \"x\" ; touch INJECTED ; echo \"\""`, `injected:true`.
  Under `--read-only` the same command runs inside the bwrap `--ro-bind` sandbox (tools.ts:715-742), so writes fail there (R4/R4b).
- Impact: complete review-mode bypass via one argument; also lets any prompt-injected model run arbitrary shell in auto mode under the guise of "tests".
- Remediation: quote the filter with a proper shell-escape (or pass argv to the runner without a shell) and reject filters containing shell
  metacharacters; treat `run_tests` as `proc` requiring approval in review mode (approve the resolved command once per session).
- Acceptance test: R9 rig → `approval.request` with `tool:"run_tests"` showing the resolved command; with approval granted, `INJECTED` is not created and the filter appears literally in the test runner's argv.
- Dependencies: T-01. Not addressed on any branch.

### T-07 A quarantined secret placeholder is rehydrated into public-destination tool arguments (`search_web`)
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Trigger: a secret the egress classifier recognises (e.g. `sk-…`) is read by a tool; the model sees `[NEXUS_SEC_REF_…]`; the model calls `search_web` with that placeholder.
- Expected: placeholders are rehydrated only for local sinks (file writes, local commands); public sinks keep the placeholder or are refused.
- Observed: every tool call's args are restored first — 3727938:cli/src/agent.ts:2484-2490 (`getVault().restore(serialized)`) — and the spine
  egress hook only re-checks `fetch_web`, `browser_navigate` and remote MCP (agent.ts:668-728); everything else, including `search_web`, falls into
  the "authorized local sink" rehydration branch (agent.ts:730-742). `search_web` sends the query to `SEARXNG_URL` or DuckDuckGo (search_web.ts:21-50, 94).
  R12 (SEARXNG_URL pointed at a local capture server): `modelSawRawKey:false, placeholder:"[NEXUS_SEC_REF_a1b9…]", searchQueriesReceived:["/search?q=error REDACTED&format=json"], rawKeyLeftHost:true`.
- Impact: the vault's guarantee (model never sees, secret never leaves) is inverted: the model can cause the real key to be published to a third-party search engine without ever knowing it.
- Remediation: classify each tool's sink (`HOST_LOCAL` vs external) in the capability registry; rehydrate only for local sinks; for external
  sinks run `evaluateEgress` on the args and refuse if any placeholder or secret is present.
- Acceptance test: R12 rig → capture server receives the placeholder (or no request), never the raw key; a `write_file` with the placeholder still writes the real value locally.
- Dependencies: none.

### T-08 Secret redaction misses common formats and durable stores keep them in plaintext (sessions, diffs, audit log, task state, flight log)
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches (persistence and egress code identical in the relevant files)
- Trigger: a workspace file contains secrets in common formats; the agent reads it (`read_file`, `cat`) and writes a copy.
- Expected: no plaintext secret in `~/.nexus/**` or `<repo>/.nexus/**`; common formats tokenized before reaching the model.
- Observed (R11, `recordFlight:true`): sent to model in plaintext — unquoted `DB_PASSWORD=REDACTED, URL credentials `postgres://admin:<pw>@…`, a JWT
  (an `sk-…`, `ghp_…` and AWS secret were tokenized). Persisted in plaintext:
  `~/.nexus/audit.log` (URL password, JWT), `~/.nexus/sessions/<id>.json` and `~/.nexus/tasks/task-*.json` (unquoted password, URL password, JWT),
  `~/.nexus/sessions/<id>.diffs/*.diff` (URL password, JWT **and the AWS secret** — the diff store applies weaker redaction than the egress path),
  `<repo>/.nexus/flights/*.flightlog` (unquoted password, URL password, JWT). Classifier: core/egress.ts (deterministic/contextual/entropy passes, ~lines 280-360);
  UI redaction is a separate, different regex set (cli/src/ui.ts:6-13).
- Impact: credentials accumulate in operator-home files that are later exported/shared (session export, audit, flight logs) and go to cloud models.
- Remediation: one canonical classifier for egress, UI and persistence; add URL userinfo, JWT (`eyJ…\.eyJ…\.`), unquoted `*_(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD)=` rules;
  route the diff writer and audit log through `redactForPersistence`.
- Acceptance test: R11 rig → `persistedHome` and `persistedRepoNexus` empty; `sentToModel` all false.
- Dependencies: T-05.

### T-09 Objective ledger accepts `verified` from any passing `run_tests`, including a filtered run that executes no tests
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Trigger: model edits, runs `run_tests {filter:"no-such-test-name"}` (passes because nothing runs), then `update_requirements` R1/R2 `verified`.
- Expected: `verified` binds only to the configured/authoritative verifier (unfiltered), as the turn predicate does.
- Observed: `currentPassingAttempt` accepts any PASSED attempt with matching workspace state (agent.ts:1480-1491); `recordAttempt` stores
  whatever `parsed.command` ran (agent.ts:2622-2636). R10: `reqs:[{R1, verified, verifiedBy:"npm test -- -t \"no-such-test-name\""}, {R2, verified, …}]`
  while the full suite would fail; the turn itself correctly ended `TURN ENDED - UNVERIFIED (VERIFICATION_NOT_RUN)`.
- Impact: the ledger (shown to operator and model, persisted, used for continuation) claims operator requirements are verified when they are not;
  the turn outcome is not fooled, so this is a misleading-state defect, not a false completion. Descoping is correctly operator-only (objective.ts:29-35, 242-256, 349-353).
- Remediation: record attempts with `filtered:true` when `args.filter` is set and refuse them for `verified`; or bind `verified` to `discoverVerifier()`'s command.
- Acceptance test: R10 rig → `update_requirements verified` rejected with a "filtered run" error; R1/R2 stay `implemented`.
- Dependencies: T-06.

### T-10 Read-only blocks of `run_tests` surface as a test failure; `write_file` always reports `"overwritten"`
- Priority: P3
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Observed: under `--read-only` `run_tests` runs in the read-only sandbox and is reported as `"Test suite failed: Errors encountered"` (R4/R4b),
  not as a policy block, which invites the model to "fix" tests. `write_file` computes status after writing
  (core/src/file_ops.rs:231 `if target.exists()`), so new files are reported `"status": "overwritten"` (R10, I2, I5 outputs).
- Remediation: detect read-only in `run_tests` and return a policy error up front; compute `existed` before opening the file.
- Acceptance test: read-only `run_tests` → error text contains "read-only"; `write_file` of a new path → `"created"`.

### T-11 Workspace confinement is lexical in TS and check-then-act in Rust (TOCTOU), with an outside zero-byte create on symlink swap
- Priority: P3
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK
- Affects: all three branches
- Observed: TS `confine` uses `path.resolve`/`path.relative` only (core/authority.ts:267-370), no realpath. The real guard is Rust
  `resolve_safe_path` (file_ops.rs:651-711; canonicalises existing targets/ancestors, rejects escaping symlinks, `..` popping past root) plus
  post-open `/proc/self/fd` verification in `write_file`/`edit_file` (file_ops.rs:55-75, 221, 533, 606) — this is good. Residual races:
  `write_file` opens with `create(true)` before verifying the descriptor, so a component swapped to an outside symlink between check and open creates an
  empty outside file before the write is refused; `create_dir_all(parent)` (file_ops.rs:206-211) can create outside directories under a racing swap;
  `delete_file` canonicalises then `remove_*` by path (file_ops.rs:630-648). Requires a concurrent local attacker; not reproduced.
- Remediation: open relative to a workspace dirfd with `openat2(RESOLVE_BENEATH|RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS)` (Linux) for create/delete.
- Acceptance test: Rust unit test that swaps a parent dir for an outside symlink between resolve and open (via a test hook) → no outside file created.

### T-12 Default operating mode executes edits, deletes and shell commands with no approval; `fetch_web`/`search_web`/`browser_*` are never gated
- Priority: P2
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK (product decision to surface)
- Affects: all three branches, installed runtime
- Observed: sidecar mode is `review` only with `--approve` (sidecar.ts:792, 800); REPL `autoApprove = true` by default (repl.ts:68, index.ts:112).
  Network tools are `mutating:false` (capabilities.ts: `net_fetch`, `net_search`, `browser_*`), allowed in read-only and never approval-gated, and no
  domain allowlist exists unless `.nexus-security.json` sets one (security.ts:44-74). `isSafeOutboundUrl` checks only the initial URL; `fetch` follows redirects
  (tools.ts:38-90, 618-623; no `redirect` option). Workspace content can thus be sent to arbitrary hosts by a prompt-injected model.
- Remediation: make review the default for new workspaces or show the mode prominently at start; gate network egress tools in review mode;
  set `redirect:"manual"` and re-validate each hop.
- Acceptance test: `fetch_web` to a URL that 302-redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` is refused; review mode asks before `fetch_web`.

## Findings — Area 5 (inference compatibility and recovery)

Rig: `assess/ti/main/cli/test/zz_infer_repro.test.ts` — own raw OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (arbitrary bodies, status, headers, chunked bytes,
socket reset), real `SidecarServer` + `ApplicationCore` agent loop, recovery env shortened (`LOCAL_LLM_RECOVERY_*`). client.ts, parser.ts and
provider_recovery.ts are byte-identical on main, feat/tui-surface and fix/context-convergence (`git diff` empty).

### I-01 Tool calls are extracted from `<think>` reasoning and executed — a deletion the model explicitly declined was performed
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches, installed runtime (re-run on tui: identical)
- Trigger: a reasoning model (DeepSeek-R1/Qwen style) replies `<think>I could run {"name":"delete_file","arguments":{"path":"important.txt"}} but that would destroy data, so I will not.</think>The file looks fine; no changes needed.`
- Expected: no tool runs; text in reasoning is never an instruction.
- Observed: parser step 6 "Rescue tool call if accidentally placed inside DeepSeek <think> reasoning" (3727938:cli/src/parser.ts:314-335) turns any
  balanced JSON with a `name` in the reasoning into a tool call. I5c: `toolStarts:[{tool:"delete_file",subject:"important.txt"}]`, `toolEnds:[{success:true}]`, `importantExists:false`.
- Impact: destructive actions from hypothetical reasoning, without approval in auto mode (and in review mode for `delete_file`, see T-01).
- Remediation: remove the reasoning rescue; if kept, only for a model profile known to emit calls in `<think>`, and never for mutating tools.
- Acceptance test: I5c → `toolStarts:[]`, `important.txt` present, turn completes with the final text.

### I-02 Lenient JSON repair silently rewrites file content (`None`→`null`, `True`→`true`, trailing commas removed)
- Priority: P1
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Trigger: tool-call arguments that are invalid JSON only because of raw newlines inside strings (the most common local-model artifact), with code content.
- Expected: either an exact repair (escape control characters only) or a rejection asking the model to resend.
- Observed: `repairJson` applies global regex rewrites to the whole text, inside string values too (parser.ts:33-43: Python literals,
  trailing commas, unquoted keys) before the control-character pass (parser.ts:64-96), which is built on the already-rewritten text.
  Probe P1 (`parseModelResponse` with args `{"path":"m.py","content":"x = None\nif True:\n    items = [1, 2,]\n"}` with raw newlines):
  `{"path":"m.py","content":"x = null\nif true:\n    items = [1, 2]\n"}` — that is what `write_file` would write. When the rewrite breaks
  quoting instead (I1b, content containing `{a: 1}`), the call fails with a misleading `FAIL-002: Missing required parameter 'path'`.
- Impact: silent corruption of Python/JS/YAML content written by local models; hard to notice because the write "succeeds".
- Remediation: run the string-aware control-character escape first on the original text; apply structural repairs only outside string literals (tokenizer-based); on any repair, record it in the tool receipt.
- Acceptance test: P1 → content identical to the intended text with `None`/`True`/`[1, 2,]` preserved.

### I-03 An empty assistant reply is reported as a completed turn
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches, installed runtime (re-run on tui: identical)
- Trigger: stream completes (`finish_reason:"stop"`, `[DONE]`) with no content and no tool calls; the non-streaming re-request (client.ts:1307-1311) also returns `content:""`.
- Expected: a failed/incomplete turn ("model returned no output"), optionally with one bounded retry.
- Observed: I3: 2 requests (`stream:[true,false]`), `TURN ENDED - NO CHANGES TO VERIFY`, `execution=COMPLETED outcome=NOT_REQUIRED modelStop=FINAL_TEXT`, empty final text.
- Impact: operators see success for a turn that did nothing; common with overloaded local servers and template mismatches.
- Remediation: in the turn loop, treat `toolCalls.length === 0 && !text.trim()` as `modelStop: EMPTY_OUTPUT` → execution FAILED (agent.ts near 3158, subagent already does this at 3640-3644).
- Acceptance test: I3 → `execution=FAILED`, reason names empty output.

### I-04 Text that merely contains JSON with a `name` field is executed as a tool call
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Trigger: final answer quoting a `package.json` (`{"name":"my-app","version":"1.0.0",…}`).
- Observed: parser step 5 (parser.ts:291-312) accepts any balanced object with `name|tool|action`. I5b: tool `my-app` dispatched → `FAIL-001 … not registered`,
  an extra inference request, the answer is re-generated. Combined with I-01, a quoted example like `{"name":"delete_file",…}` in prose would run.
- Remediation: only accept embedded calls whose name is an offered tool and whose shape is `{name, arguments}`; skip steps 4-6 when the model/provider supports native tool calls.
- Acceptance test: I5b → no tool dispatched, one request, final text kept.

### I-05 Provider context-length errors end the turn; llama.cpp's error shape is not recognised as capacity; no reactive compaction
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Observed: I6 (OpenAI shape, `code:"context_length_exceeded"`) → classified `CAPACITY_REJECTED`, `NOT_EXECUTED`, then `TURN FAILED … HTTP 400` after 1 request.
  I6b (llama.cpp server shape: `type:"exceed_context_size_error"`, message "exceeds the available context size", `n_ctx`) → `REQUEST_REJECTED`
  (the body regex at core/provider_recovery.ts:106 lacks "context size"). No code in agent.ts handles `CAPACITY_REJECTED` (grep: no match), so neither
  compaction-and-retry nor `n_ctx` learning happens; pre-flight admission (`ContextBudgetError`) exists but depends on a configured/learned limit.
- Impact: long sessions against local servers with a smaller real `n_ctx` than configured fail hard instead of compacting.
- Remediation: add `exceed_context_size_error`/"context size"/`n_ctx` to capacity classification; on CAPACITY_REJECTED compact once and resubmit, and lower the learned context limit from `n_ctx`.
- Acceptance test: I6b → classified CAPACITY_REJECTED; with a script that accepts the second (compacted, shorter) request, the turn completes.

### I-06 SSE lines `data:` without the optional space are ignored, failing the turn
- Priority: P2
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Affects: all three branches
- Observed: the parser accepts only `data: ` (client.ts:1177, 1181); the SSE spec makes the space optional. I7 → 3 submissions, `stream_incomplete`,
  `Provider recovery exhausted … replay budget (2) is spent`, `TURN FAILED`.
- Remediation: accept `/^data:\s?/` and `data:[DONE]`.
- Acceptance test: I7 → turn completes with text "nospace".

### I-07 Provider-reported usage is ignored for plain endpoints; inference receipts exist only for connected providers
- Priority: P2
- Label: SOURCE-SUPPORTED RISK (partly observed)
- Affects: all three branches
- Observed: `withReceipt` returns early when `!this.conn.providerId` (client.ts:520-521) and stream usage is captured only into `this.pending`, which is
  set only for providers (client.ts:1166, 1201-1205); the agent uses reported usage only when `getProviderId()` is set, else an estimate (agent.ts:3107-3123).
  I10 sent a `usage` chunk (1234/56) from a plain endpoint; the turn projection has no usage fields and nothing records it.
- Impact: for local-first users (LM Studio/vLLM/llama.cpp via `--endpoint`) token accounting is estimated and there is no receipt trail.
- Remediation: always capture `usage`, `id`, `model` from responses and write receipts with `providerId:"endpoint:<origin>"`.
- Acceptance test: I10 → a receipt in the usage ledger with `usage.inputTokens:1234` and session totals including 1234.

### I-08 Malformed tool-call JSON yields a misleading error to the model
- Priority: P3
- Label: REPRODUCED DEFECT
- Observed: I1 (`{"path":"a.txt","content":"hello"` unterminated) → args become `{raw:…}` (agent.ts:2472-2480) → `FAIL-002: Malformed arguments: Missing required parameter 'path'`.
  The model is not told its JSON was invalid; it recovered here (next reply was text), but local models often loop on this.
- Remediation: return "arguments were not valid JSON: <parse error>; resend the call" when `raw` is set.
- Acceptance test: I1 → tool message contains "not valid JSON".

## What is solid (with evidence)
- Read-only command execution is defence-in-depth: authority admission rejects shell metacharacters and allowlists inspection commands
  (core/authority.ts:43-130, 213-230), the bridge applies a second allowlist (tools.ts:31-32, 445-463), and every read-only command runs in bwrap/docker with
  `--ro-bind` and no network or is refused if no sandbox exists (tools.ts:715-742, sandbox.ts:126-180). R4/R4b: `npm test` mutates normally but not under read-only;
  R5: `rg --pre ./pre.sh` refused; R7: `delete_file`, `manage_knowledge` denied with AUTH-009.
- Rust path confinement canonicalises targets/ancestors, rejects escaping and broken symlinks and verifies opened descriptors (file_ops.rs:55-75, 651-711; unit tests 1096-1131).
- Streaming: UTF-8 decoding with `stream:true` (I8: "héllo 🙂 wörld" split mid-emoji intact), incomplete streams detected (no `finish_reason`/`[DONE]`),
  `finish_reason=length` refuses partial tool ar
